plain_english: The path of art will be spoken according to glorious Shambhava knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: kalādhvā vakṣyate śrīmacchāṃbhavājñānusārataḥ

plain_english: As in the previously stated middle of the world, after each group follows its own, a separate principle is said to be called.
sanskrit_cite: yathā pūrvoktabhuvanamadhye nijanijaṃ gaṇam anuyatparato bhinnaṃ tattvaṃ nāmeti bhaṇyate

plain_english: Thus, among those principles too, that which is of the nature of approach to its own class and separated from the other class is called kala in the teaching of Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: tathā teṣvapi tattveṣu svavarge@nugamātmakam vyāvṛttaṃ paravargācca kaleti śivaśāsane

plain_english: Some say that this power, again, is the very subtle power within the principles; it is called kalā, as the bearer in earth.
sanskrit_cite: kecidāhuḥ punaryāsau śaktirantaḥ susūkṣmikā tattvānāṃ sā kaletyuktā dharaṇyāṃ dhārikā yathā

plain_english: Here the thing does not appear divided in two alternatives, because a universal is not accepted as following, unlike the Nyāyikas and others.
sanskrit_cite: atra pakṣadvaye vastu na bhinnaṃ bhāsate yataḥ anugāmi na sāmānyamiṣṭaṃ naiyāyikādivat

plain_english: Others say that at the beginning of initiation, for the purpose of easy collection, Shiva devised a class called kala, which is samaya-dependent.
sanskrit_cite: anye vadanti dīkṣādau sukhasaṃgrahaṇārthataḥ śivena kalpito vargaḥ kaleti samayāśrayaḥ

plain_english: The covenant made by the God of gods does not reach ultimate reality; yet it is not false, and no other covenant arises.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtaśca devadevena samayo@paramārthatām na gacchatīti nāsatyo na cānyasamayodayaḥ

plain_english: Cessation belongs to the earth-principle, establishment to the manifest perceptible domain, knowledge to the end of night, and peace to the end of power; this egg is four.
sanskrit_cite: nivṛttiḥ pṛthivītattve pratiṣṭhāvyaktagocare vidyā niśānte śāntā ca śaktyante@ṇḍamidaṃ catuḥ

plain_english: In the Shiva-principle beyond peace, supreme Shiva is beyond kala; here there is no classification, convention, or even counting.
sanskrit_cite: śāntātītā śive tattve kalātītaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ nahyatra vargīkaraṇaṃ samayaḥ kalanāpi vā

plain_english: It is united in all directions in the abode of the expansion of freedom; but from freedom its own form does not fall away from the nature of the knower.
sanskrit_cite: yujyate sarvatodikkaṃ svātantryollāsadhāmani svātantryāttu nijaṃ rūpaṃ boddhṛdharmādavicyutam

plain_english: For the establishment of ultimate reality through instruction and immersion in that, the god who brings understanding is clearly manifested.
sanskrit_cite: upadeśatadāveśaparamārthatvasiddhaye bodhyatāmānayandevaḥ sphuṭameva vibhāvyate

plain_english: Because even in the Shiva principle a union of kalās is declared; and the cosmic egg is named the cause of the establishment of world-divisions.
sanskrit_cite: yato@taḥ śivatattve@pi kalāsaṃgatirucyate aṇḍaṃ ca nāma bhuvanavibhāgasthitikāraṇam

plain_english: They call 'covering' that which ends in power, as long as it exists; although before, even in the principle called Śiva, there is the world-path.
sanskrit_cite: prāhurāvaraṇaṃ tacca śaktyantaṃ yāvadasti hi yadyapi prāk śivākhye@pi tattve bhuvanapaddhatiḥ

plain_english: It has been said; yet even in the unobstructed, there is no occurrence of veiling in this. But thus, having left earth, [one is] in the powers of prakṛti and māyā.
sanskrit_cite: uktā tathāpyapratighe nāsminnāvṛtisaṃbhavaḥ nanvevaṃ dharaṇīṃ muktvā śaktau prakṛtimāyayoḥ

plain_english: Even in non-obstruction, how does the egg originate? Here our teachers say it is the five beginning with earth.
sanskrit_cite: api cāpratighatve@pi kathamaṇḍasya saṃbhavaḥ atrāsmadguravaḥ prāhuryatpṛthivyādipañcakam

plain_english: This appears directly, and nothing else exists; in measurability, gross and subtle distinctions arise through instrumentality.
sanskrit_cite: pratyakṣamidamābhāti tato@nyannāsti kiṃcana meyatve sthūlasūkṣmatvānmānatve karaṇatvataḥ

plain_english: From the exultation of the agent, in the state of agency, the thirty principles are clearly set forth as having the nature of difference; their non-difference is considered night.
sanskrit_cite: kartṛtollāsataḥ kartṛbhāve sphuṭatayoditam triṃśattattvaṃ vibhedātma tadabhedo niśā matā

plain_english: When distinctions such as effectness and instrumentness dissolve, in the state of supreme independent expansion, they sang the fivefold ending in Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: kāryatvakaraṇatvādivibhāgagalane sati vikāsotkasvatantratve śivāntaṃ pañcakaṃ jaguḥ

plain_english: It is declared abundantly in the glorious Kalottara and other texts; thus these five principles indeed pervade the whole world.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmatkālottarādau ca kathitaṃ bhūyasā tathā pañcaitāni tu tattvāni yairvyāptamakhilaṃ jagat

plain_english: In the five-mantra body, sadyojata and the rest are said up to Ishana; there, from earth to the end of sky.
sanskrit_cite: pañcamantratanau tena sadyojātādi bhaṇyate īśānāntaṃ tatra tatra dharādigaganāntakam

plain_english: From the Shiva principle comes the void beyond void, which would be unattached; but the Shiva principle itself is the self of all non-difference, independent, and beautiful consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: śivatattvamataḥ śūnyātiśūnyaṃ syādanāśri[vṛ]tam yattu sarvāvibhāgātma svatantraṃ bodhasundaram

plain_english: But the thirty-seventh they call the principle named Para-Shiva; even that, by the stated method, is imagined in the knowable state there.
sanskrit_cite: saptatriṃśaṃ tu tatprāhustattvaṃ paraśivābhidham tasyāpyuktanayādvedyabhāve@tra parikalpite

plain_english: When it abides unbounded, that is called the thirty-eighth; there is no regress, and thus it would be seen by great souls.
sanskrit_cite: yadāste hyanavacchinnaṃ tadaṣṭātriṃśamucyate na cānavasthā hyevaṃ syāddṛśyatāṃ hi mahātmabhiḥ

plain_english: What is knowable shines; when it disappears, what shines forth is tattva; thus the thirty-six shine in the heart.
sanskrit_cite: yadvedyaṃ kiṃcidābhāti tatkṣaye yatprakāśate tattattvamiti nirṇītaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ hṛdi bhāsate

plain_english: Then what? Not something or? The body, in dependence on desire for something, is consciousness-bliss-independent one-form? That, thus, in teaching.
sanskrit_cite: tatkiṃ na kiṃcidvā kiṃcidityākāṅkṣāvaśe vapuḥ cidānandasvatantraikarūpaṃ taditi deśane

plain_english: The thirty-seventh shines equally; there is no other expectation there; and that too is an established knowability where it shines; that is made of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: saptatriṃśaṃ samābhāti tatrākāṅkṣā ca nāparā taccāpi klṛptavedyatvaṃ yatra bhāti sa cinmayaḥ

plain_english: He too is taught by meditation as the thirty-eighth; if indeed, then the thirty-seventh would become again.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭātriṃśattamaḥ so@pi bhāvanāyopadiśyate yadi nāma tataḥ saptatriṃśa eva punarbhavet

plain_english: The nature of non-difference, independence, consciousness-fullness, and the like is indeed the same; making something known is only more than that, because...
sanskrit_cite: avibhāgasvatantratvacinmayatvādidharmatā samaiva vedyīkaraṇaṃ kevalaṃ tvadhikaṃ yataḥ

plain_english: On earth, at the end of the guna-tattva and at the end of maya, they are situated gradually: smell, taste, and form within, by the sequence of subtle beings, but...
sanskrit_cite: dharāyāṃ guṇatattvānte māyānte kramaśaḥ sthitāḥ gandho raso rūpamantaḥ sūkṣmabhāvakrameṇa tu

plain_english: Thus, with the doctrine established, even at the end of the śakti-tattva there is some subtle touch, which yogis always desire.
sanskrit_cite: iti sthite naye śaktitattvānte@pyasti saukṣmyabhāk sparśaḥ ko@pi sadā yasmai yoginaḥ spṛhayālavaḥ

plain_english: But at the end of that touch, awareness, shaped as pure consciousness-space, in which one is established, approaches the supreme self-luminous.
sanskrit_cite: tatsparśānte tu saṃvittiḥ śuddhacidvyomarūpiṇī yasyāṃ rūḍhaḥ samabhyeti svaprakāśātmikāṃ parām

plain_english: Therefore from the bindu comes sound; from that comes form; from that comes taste; thus is said of agitation-nature in spanda; but touch is not so.
sanskrit_cite: ato vindurato nādo rūpamasmādato rasaḥ ityuktaṃ kṣobhakatvena spande sparśastu no tathā

plain_english: The opinion of Caitanya-Maheśa, which Śrī formerly spoke, is a nourishing sustainer, enlightener, purifier, and giver of space.
sanskrit_cite: mataṃ caitanmaheśasya śrīpūrve yadabhāṣata dhārikāpyāyinī boddhrī pavitrī cāvakāśadā

plain_english: By these words dealing with nivṛtti and the rest, one's own body is the five-element rule that has been stated; now the three principles are described.
sanskrit_cite: ebhiḥ śabdairvyavaharan nivṛttyādernijaṃ vapuḥ pañcatattvavidhiḥ proktastritattvamadhunocyate

plain_english: The self reaches only up to vijnanakala; beyond that, in the remainder ending in vidyesvara, Shiva may be in three principles or in one principle, and Shiva is supreme.
sanskrit_cite: vijñānākalaparyantamātmā vidyeśvarāntakam śeṣe śivastritattve syādekatattve śivaḥ param

plain_english: These two differences are produced solely by tattva-difference; thus, in the tattva-adhvan there is loss, but there is no loss from the establishment of the six adhvans.
sanskrit_cite: imau bhedāvubhau tattvabhedamātrakṛtāviti tattvādhvaivāyamitthaṃ ca na ṣaḍadhvasthiteḥ kṣatiḥ

plain_english: Nature, puruṣa, time, māyā, vidyeśa, sauśiva, and Śiva are principles; even in the nine-principle rule, there is the form of the essence-sacrifice.
sanskrit_cite: prakṛt pumānyatiḥ kālo māyā vidyeśasauśivau śivaśca navatattve@pi vidhau tattvādhvarūpatā

plain_english: Thus, in the procedure called eighteen, the wise would state the law: wherever there is desire for enjoyment, it is applied according to its predominance and usefulness.
sanskrit_cite: evamaṣṭādaśākhye@pi vidhau nyāyaṃ vadetsudhīḥ yatra yatra hi bhogecchā tatprādhānyopayogataḥ

plain_english: And from other inner contemplation, initiation has endless distinctions; by that, from thirty-six until the rite of the single principle becomes.
sanskrit_cite: anyāntarbhāvanātaśca dīkṣānantavibhedabhāk tena ṣaṭtriṃśato yāvadekatattvavidhirbhavet

plain_english: This truth-path was indeed spoken by God, in detail and in brief; this one truth-rule is for the well-awakened guru.
sanskrit_cite: tattvādhvaiva sa devena prokto vyāsasamāsataḥ ekatattvavidhiścaiṣa suprabuddhaṃ guruṃ prati

plain_english: The disciple is delighted by Shambhu because the hope of enjoyment has departed; difference is expanded by Shambhu's self-willed power.
sanskrit_cite: śiṣyaṃ ca gatabhogāśamuditaḥ śaṃbhunā yataḥ bhedaṃ visphārya visphārya śaktyā svacchandarūpayā

plain_english: The Lord always rests in the non-different self; thus the threefold path differs as gross, subtle, and supreme.
sanskrit_cite: svātmanyabhinne bhagavānnityaṃ viśramayan sthitaḥ itthaṃ tryātmādhvano bhedaḥ sthūlasūkṣmaparatvataḥ

plain_english: The one who has entered the measurable part is called the city-principle-phase self; now the form situated in the maternal part is determined in three ways.
sanskrit_cite: meyabhāgagataḥ proktaḥ puratattvakalātmakaḥ adhunā mātṛbhāgasthaṃ rūpaṃ tredhā nirūpyate

plain_english: The measure-natured form of the path that reaches the mother-part is called a word, because comprehension merges into self-nature.
sanskrit_cite: yatpramāṇātmakaṃ rūpamadhvano mātṛbhāgagam padaṃ hyavagamātmatvasamāveśāttaducyate

plain_english: That indeed is the word, the mantra, fallen from agitation, when the secret-speaker becomes silent and established, because the mother.
sanskrit_cite: tadeva ca padaṃ mantraḥ prakṣobhātpracyutaṃ yadā guptabhāṣī yato mātā tūṣṇīṃbhūto vyavasthitaḥ

plain_english: Nevertheless, he does not abandon the form of the self of reflection; by that he is the self of measure and reflection, not like a man subject to agitation.
sanskrit_cite: tathāpi na vimarśātma rūpaṃ tyajati tena saḥ pramāṇātmavimarśātmā mānavatkṣobhabhāṅnatu

plain_english: In the Trika teaching, the mantras and words spoken by him have an own form that is indeed undivided, supreme in agitated non-vibration.
sanskrit_cite: mantrāṇāṃ ca padānāṃ ca tenoktaṃ trikaśāsane abhinnameva svaṃ rūpaṃ niḥspandakṣobhite param

plain_english: When indifference is abandoned and agitation descends, the path of phonemes comes into play; in the Mother-portion that valid cognition would be the one stated before.
sanskrit_cite: audāsīnyaparityāge prakṣobhānavarohaṇe varṇādhvā mātṛbhāge syāt pūrvaṃ yā kathitā pramā

plain_english: She is, however, non-different because of her full essence; therefore, in truth, each letter is one, beginning from patience.
sanskrit_cite: sā tu pūrṇasvarūpatvādavibhāgamayī yataḥ tata ekaikavarṇatvaṃ tattve tattve kṣamāditaḥ

plain_english: Having done [the rite] in supreme Śaiva, the sixteen-syllabled [mantra] is declared from visarga; there, so much śakti-vibration is determined beforehand.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtvā śaive pare proktāḥ ṣoḍaśārṇā visargataḥ tatra śaktiparispandastāvān prāk ca nirūpitaḥ

plain_english: Now everything is summed up: in bliss-consciousness one holds a single sixteen-fold mantra syllable or word; and cessation is another mantra word—truth-syllable, fire-eye, city-arrow-essence.
sanskrit_cite: saṃkalayyocyate sarvamadhunā sukhasaṃvide padamantravarṇamekaṃ puraṣoḍaśakaṃ dhareti ca nivṛttiḥ tattvārṇamagninayanaṃ rasaśarapuramastramantrapadamanyā

plain_english: The sage-principle syllable is a two-foot mantra; the fire-syllable principle is a one-foot mantra; and the army-world is thus the fourth.
sanskrit_cite: munitattvārṇaṃ dvikapadamantraṃ vasvakṣibhuvanamaparakalā agnyarṇatattvamekakapadamantraṃ sainyabhuvanamiti turyā

plain_english: Sixteen letters and one pada-mantra principle, beyond peace, were spoken by Abhinavagupta to the three noble ones for the disciples' summary.
sanskrit_cite: ṣoḍaśa varṇāḥ padamantratattvamekaṃ ca śāntyatīteyam abhinavaguptenāryātrayamuktaṃ saṃgrahāya śiṣyebhyaḥ

plain_english: That entire path, possessing the mode of non-difference from Bhairava, shines by attaining autonomy from its freedom.
sanskrit_cite: so@yaṃ samasta evādhvā bhairavābhedavṛttimān tatsvātantryātsvatantratvamaśnuvāno@vabhāsate

plain_english: For thus, abiding in mother-form, the mantra-path is determined; for thus, when the expressible state is swallowed by consciousness-reflection.
sanskrit_cite: tathāhi mātṛrūpastho mantrādhveti nirūpitaḥ tathāhi cidvimarśena grastā vācyadaśā yadā

plain_english: Intent on protecting meditation dependent on Shiva's knowledge and action, from skill and eagerness in the play of unlimited multitudes of powers.
sanskrit_cite: śivajñānakriyāyattamananatrāṇatatparā aśeṣaśaktipaṭalīlīlālāmpaṭyapāṭavāt

plain_english: Fallen from measure-made form and gone into the consciousness-mantra paths, having attained measure-form, the path goes to the state of word-self.
sanskrit_cite: cyutā mānamayādrūpāt saṃvinmantrādhvatāṃ gatā pramāṇarūpatāmetya prayātyadhvā padātmatām

plain_english: Thus indeed, the mother's rest assembles many letters; collision and sequential process are speech-nature indeed, that.
sanskrit_cite: tathā hi māturviśrāntirvarṇānsaṃghaṭya tānbahūn saṃghaṭṭanaṃ ca kramikaṃ saṃjalpātmakameva tat

plain_english: Imagination's own form is clearly made of enjoyment-entrancement; therefore our teacher sang it as the form of validity.
sanskrit_cite: vikalpasya svakaṃ rūpaṃ bhogāveśamayaṃ sphuṭam ataḥ pramāṇatārūpaṃ padamasmadgururjagau

plain_english: Without abandoning entry into the form of pramana, measurability...
sanskrit_cite: pramāṇarūpatāveśamaparityajya meyatām

plain_english: The path that proceeds by calculation from yoga is declared to consist of parts; in pure union of measurability it has a share of subtle and gross.
sanskrit_cite: gacchankalanayā yogādadhvā proktaḥ kalātmakaḥ śuddhe prameyatāyoge sūkṣmasthūlatvabhāgini

plain_english: In the state of the reality-path and world-path, the guru follows in order the form situated above of the measurable, the means, and the knowers.
sanskrit_cite: tattvādhvabhuvanādhvatve krameṇānusaredguruḥ prameyamānamātṝṇāṃ yadrūpamupari sthitam

plain_english: Let the sound-self indeed be seen by yogins who taste rest in rising consciousness, abiding in meditation on the supreme self only.
sanskrit_cite: pramātmātra sthito@dhvāyaṃ varṇātmā dṛśyatāṃ kila ucchalatsaṃvidāmātraviśrāntyāsvādayoginaḥ

plain_english: From the power of all designations, unrestrained powers are created; in the meaning that arises together with the self, they extend as far as earth.
sanskrit_cite: sarvābhidhānasāmarthyādaniyantritaśaktayaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svātmasahotthe@rthe dharāparyantabhāgini

plain_english: Considering in the ground of consciousness, those streams of letters bear consciousness as true valid cognition, without distinction among so many objects.
sanskrit_cite: āmṛśantaḥ svacidbhūmau tāvato@rthānabhedataḥ varṇaughāste pramārūpāṃ satyāṃ bibhrati saṃvidam

plain_english: Children and animals are also cognizers; even those who share no convention have, through innate refinement, this very self-awareness.
sanskrit_cite: bālāstiryakpramātāro ye@pyasaṃketabhāginaḥ te@pyakṛtrimasaṃskārasārāmenāṃ svasaṃvidam

plain_english: Having resorted to various distinct things, they attain variegated cognizer-hood; rootedness is in this natural, infinite consciousness of varṇas.
sanskrit_cite: bhinnabhinnāmupāśritya yānti citrāṃ pramātṛtām asyā cākṛtrimānantavarṇasaṃvidi rūḍhatām

plain_english: Conventions pass away; even if they enter an unsymbolic state. But without this, all conventions are made again and again.
sanskrit_cite: saṃketā yānti cette@pi yāntyasaṃketavṛttitām anayā tu vinā sarve saṃketā bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ

plain_english: By unceasingness they would make an insurmountable regress; a child is instructed there by that, through seeking convention.
sanskrit_cite: aviśrāntatayā kuryuranavasthāṃ duruttarām bālo vyutpādyate yena tatra saṃketamārgaṇāt

plain_english: Even when this is pointed out with a finger, the mind is not nonconceptual; conceptualization is rooted in word, and word lives by convention.
sanskrit_cite: aṅgulyādeśane@pyasya nāvikalpā tathā matiḥ vikalpaḥ śabdamūlaśca śabdaḥ saṃketajīvitaḥ

plain_english: By that infinite, indeed illusion-free, he who is such a group of letters, companion of the reflection of consciousness, always indeed expands.
sanskrit_cite: tenānanto hyamāyīyo yo varṇagrāma īdṛśaḥ saṃvidvimarśasacivaḥ sadaiva sa hi jṛmbhate

plain_english: Since indeed the māyic colors spread birth, and those are determined as potency within the māyic colors.
sanskrit_cite: yata eva ca māyīyā varṇāḥ sūtiṃ vitenire ye ca māyīyavarṇeṣu vīryatvena nirūpitāḥ

plain_english: They are indifferent to convention; let their proceeding be accepted, for when others' words are heard, one's own is covered.
sanskrit_cite: saṃketanirapekṣāste prameti parigṛhyatām tathā hi paravākyeṣu śruteṣvāvriyate nijā

plain_english: Whose valid knowledge is dull does not approach there for that purpose; motherhood; the parrot-child indeed reads the supreme, a one-share-holder in that order.
sanskrit_cite: pramā yasya jaḍo@sau no tatrārthe@bhyeti mātṛtām śukavatsa paṭhatyeva paraṃ tatkramitaikabhāk

plain_english: But indeed, whose knowerhood is from the gain of independence? In the gain of self-statement pramā, self-pramā-awareness is from the exposure and refutation of opponents.
sanskrit_cite: svātantryalābhataḥ svākyapramālābhe tu boddhṛtā yasya hi svapramābodho vipakṣodbhedanigrahāt

plain_english: In the heap of letters beginning with a sentence, the knower becomes master in his own form, as the unmade form is distinguished from that form.
sanskrit_cite: vākyādivarṇapuñje sve sa pramātā vaśībhavet yathā yathā cākṛtakaṃ tadrūpamatiricyate

plain_english: Thus wonder is perceived in gradation: immersed within the first mayic letter, and likewise in each subsequent one.
sanskrit_cite: tathā tathā camatkāratāratamyaṃ vibhāvyate ādyāmāyīyavarṇāntarnimagne cottarottare

plain_english: In Saketa, in the immersion of the previous-previous part, those distinct in splendor are established in the splendor-self, even in the greatness of initial excess.
sanskrit_cite: sakete pūrvapūrvāṃśamajjane pratibhābhidaḥ ādyodrekamahattve@pi pratibhātmani niṣṭhitāḥ

plain_english: Certainly, they attain an abundance of poetic speech from all sides as long as they remain in the abode where convention is abandoned.
sanskrit_cite: dhruvaṃ kavitvavaktṛtvaśālitāṃ yānti sarvataḥ yāvaddhāmani saṃketanikārakalanojjhite

plain_english: One who rests in consciousness—what does he not know, what does he not do? Therefore, indeed, in the accomplishment of speech, the letters are to be worshipped.
sanskrit_cite: viśrāntaścinmaye kiṃ kiṃ na vetti kurute na vā ata eva hi vāksiddhau varṇānāṃ samupāsyatā

plain_english: Or, in the accomplishment of omniscience and the rest, what accomplishment is not made of that? This is stated by Varada in the doctrine of Śrī Siddhayogīśvarī.
sanskrit_cite: sarvajñatvādisiddhau vā kā siddhiryā na tanmayī taduktaṃ varadena śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmate

plain_english: By that hidden one, the remaining letters are protected; thus clearly, he who appears is characterized by I-ness, measurability, and knowability.
sanskrit_cite: tena guptena guptāste śeṣā varṇāstviti sphuṭam evaṃ māmātṛmānatvameyatvairyo@vabhāsate

plain_english: In the purification of one's own body, six-fold, he attains purification by the path; by the purification of one body, there indeed arises another kind.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaḍvidhaḥ svavapuḥśuddhau śuddhiṃ so@dhvādhigacchati ekena vapuṣā śuddhau tatraivānyaprakāratām

plain_english: The guru who internalizes, practices, and possesses purity and investigation...; but if the power of internalization is absent, he should purify subtly, subtly.
sanskrit_cite: antarbhāvyācarecchuddhimanusaṃdhānavān guruḥ anantarbhāvaśaktau tu sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tu śodhayet

plain_english: That which is purified, from its seed-nature, does not produce a later continuity; purification in many ways is the single continuity of attaining that enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: tadviśuddhaṃ bījabhāvāt sūte nottarasaṃtatim śodhanaṃ bahudhā tattadbhogaprāptyekatānatā

plain_english: That sovereignty, that abandonment, that knowledge of Shiva-selfhood, that absorption, that rejection—all of this occurs by order and disorder.
sanskrit_cite: tadādhipatyaṃ tattyāgastacchivātmatvavedanam tallīnatā tannirāsaḥ sarvaṃ caitatkramākramāt

plain_english: Therefore those mantras, purifying and of varied forms, spread a variegated purification in the siddhanta, vama, daksha, and related streams.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva ca te mantrāḥ śodhakāścitrarūpiṇaḥ siddhāntavāmadakṣādau citrāṃ śuddhiṃ vitanvate

plain_english: The mantras of the sequence called the unsurpassed triad are indeed all all-giving; but primacy belongs to one of them somewhere.
sanskrit_cite: anuttaratrikānāmakramamantrāstu ye kila te sarve sarvadāḥ kintu kasyācit kvāpi mukhyatā

plain_english: Therefore, in the scripture called Śrīpūrva, the arrangement of the mantras beginning with parāpara is set forth in the mantra-path, in a purifying manner.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ śodhakabhāvena śāstre śrīpūrvasaṃjñite parāparādimantrāṇāmadhvanyuktā vyavasthitiḥ

plain_english: Purifying-ness applies to the impurity of the goddesses, the triad, the three deities, and the eight faces/limbs.
sanskrit_cite: śodhakatvaṃ ca mālinyā devīnāṃ tritayasya ca devatrayasya vaktrāṇāmaṅgānāmaṣṭakasya ca

plain_english: What need of too much? In the order of door, site, support, and guru, in the rite of world-protector weapons, having omitted mantras, all is purifying.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ vātibahunā dvāravāstvādhāragurukrame lokapāstravidhau mantrān muktvā sarvaṃ viśodhakam

plain_english: And this purifiability of the path is declared, and that which is purified is said to be fit, from autonomy, in difference from Shiva, and in scripture.
sanskrit_cite: yaccaitadadhvanaḥ proktaṃ śodhyatvaṃ śoddhṛtā ca yā sā svātantryācchivābhede yuktetyuktaṃ ca śāsane

plain_english: All this indeed shines in the supreme, fixed Lord by reflection-form, not by externality, because [the reason is left implicit].
sanskrit_cite: sarvametadvibhātyeva parameśitari dhruve pratibimbasvarūpeṇa na tu bāhyatayā yataḥ

plain_english: In Shiva there is only consciousness-space; the samsarins' thought of body and the like as distinct is like the thought of snake, rope, and wave.
sanskrit_cite: cidvyomnyeva śive tattaddehādimatirīdṛśī bhinnā saṃsāriṇāṃ rajjau sarpasragvīcibuddhivat

plain_english: Since the doctrine established before the body's death is within the range of dream, in death beginning with another body, what kind is the origin of the body?
sanskrit_cite: yataḥ prāgdehamaraṇasiddhāntaḥ svapnagocaraḥ dehāntarādirmaraṇe kīdṛgvā dehasaṃbhavaḥ

plain_english: Even in a dream, particulars appear through the force of the common manifestation of mere appearance; they are not even imagined as such.
sanskrit_cite: svapne@pi pratibhāmātrasāmānyaprathanābalāt viśeṣāḥ pratibhāsante na bhāvyante@pi te yathā

plain_english: Just as some salagrama stones bear variegated forms, so too are hearts painted with variegated lines at the end of the ground of maya and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: śālagrāmopalāḥ keciccitrākṛtibhṛto yathā tathā māyādibhūmyantalekhācitrahṛdaścitaḥ

plain_english: Cities, oceans, mountains, and the like, following that will, are not self-existent; they are neither good nor bad, nor are they of the nature of cause or non-cause.
sanskrit_cite: nagarārṇavaśailādyāstadicchānuvidhāyinaḥ na svayaṃ sadasanto no kāraṇākāraṇātmakāḥ

plain_english: From the cutting off of long-established niyati and the arising of the unestablished, this independent Bhairava stands in the space of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: niyateścirarūḍhāyāḥ samucchedātpravartanāt arūḍhāyāḥ svatantro@yaṃ sthitaścidvyomabhairavaḥ

plain_english: In the circle of beings, the differentiating non-reflection 'thus I am' is the Bhairava-full part, one-cin-matra.
sanskrit_cite: ekacinmātrasaṃpūrṇabhairavābhedabhāgini evamasmītyanāmarśo bhedako bhāvamaṇḍale

plain_english: Just as another agent in a dream is not established by any means of knowledge, so everywhere let it be understood that self-awareness alone is self-established.
sanskrit_cite: sarvapramāṇairno siddhaṃ svapne kartrantaraṃ yathā svasaṃvidaḥ svasiddhāyāstathā sarvatra buddhyatām

plain_english: Who knows 'I alone am situated' would thus play in the wonderful garden-city of mind, with cities of elements, beings, and truths.
sanskrit_cite: cittacitrapurodyāne krīḍedevaṃ hi vetti yaḥ ahameva sthito bhūtabhāvatattvapurairiti

plain_english: Thus the thoughts 'I am born' and 'I am dead,' along with all varieties of birth and death, shine as self-created appearances in the wall of mind, within the unborn and immortal.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ jāto mṛto@smīti janmamṛtyuvicitratāḥ ajanmanyamṛtau bhānti cittabhittau svanirmitāḥ

plain_english: In reality, for awareness there is no place or time in either world; awareness is only of other and this world.
sanskrit_cite: parehasaṃvidāmātraṃ paralokehalokate vastutaḥ saṃvido deśaḥ kālo vā naiva kiṃcana

plain_english: This creation would not have become material if not consciousness-made; that was seen from its middle—by whom, one also earth-bearer?
sanskrit_cite: abhaviṣyadayaṃ sargo mūrtaścenna tu cinmayaḥ tadavekṣyata tanmadhyāt kenaiko@pi dharādharaḥ

plain_english: At the end of the support-and-supported order of the elements and subtle elements, the power that consists of consciousness, indeed of Śiva's form, is the supporter.
sanskrit_cite: bhūtatanmātravargāderādhārādheyatākrame ante saṃvinmayī śaktiḥ śivarūpaiva dhāriṇī

plain_english: Therefore perception itself is the doer and sustainer; she is Shiva. From that, states are there as states; power is their supporter; then.
sanskrit_cite: tasmātpratītirevetthaṃ kartrī dhartrī ca sā śivaḥ tato bhāvāstatra bhāvāḥ śaktirādhārikā tataḥ

plain_english: Even supportless, the imagined does not indeed fall downward; thus the universe, rested in its own support-power, let be considered.
sanskrit_cite: sāṃkalpikaṃ nirādhāramapi naiva patatyadhaḥ svādhāraśaktau viśrāntaṃ viśvamitthaṃ vimṛśyatām

plain_english: Of this, the convention 'dense I' and so on is indeed the state of earth and the rest up to the end; 'I am consciousness' is accomplished; Bhairava-self-ness.
sanskrit_cite: asyā ghanāhamityādirūḍhireva dharāditā yāvadante cidasmīti nirvṛttā bhairavātmatā

plain_english: Just as blue and other colors shine in a jewel and a rainbow, so in Shiva, in ultimate reality, these neither arise nor ever decay.
sanskrit_cite: maṇāvindrāyudhe bhāsa iva nīlādayaḥ śive paramārthata eṣāṃ tu nodayo na vyayaḥ kvacit

plain_english: Creation in a place or at a time is inconsistent; indeed, space and time themselves are created by God, who is consciousness itself.
sanskrit_cite: deśe kāle@tra vā sṛṣṭirityetadasamañjasam cidātmanā hi devena sṛṣṭirdikkālayorapi

plain_english: In waking, opinion is limited to a three-and-a-half-cubit range, a separate watch; in dream, directions and times are varied.
sanskrit_cite: jāgarābhimate sārdhahastatritayagocare prahare ca pṛthak svapnāścitradikkālamāninaḥ

plain_english: Therefore we do not regard even a moment as anything at all, since in one action-moment—or in a single moment—many actions occur quickly.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva kṣaṇaṃ nāma na kiṃcidapi manmahe kriyākṣaṇe vāpyekasmin bahvyaḥ saṃsyurdrutāḥ kriyāḥ

plain_english: By that, those who attained the contraction of being at the end of a moment certainly lean on an empty view by this vein.
sanskrit_cite: tena ye bhāvasaṃkocaṃ kṣaṇāntaṃ pratipedire te nūnamenayā nāḍyā śūnyadṛṣṭyavalambinaḥ

plain_english: Therefore this Lord, our Lord Shiva, lord of freedom and the rest, can make states of being void and make non-being manifest.
sanskrit_cite: tadya eṣa sato bhāvāñ śūnyīkartuṃ tathāsataḥ sphuṭīkartuṃ svatantratvādīśaḥ so@smatprabhuḥ śivaḥ

plain_english: Thus the supreme Lord, of universal form, is praised; but not the fitness of any distinct thing such as earth.
sanskrit_cite: taditthaṃ parameśāno viśvarūpaḥ pragīyate na tu bhinnasya kasyāpi dharāderupapannatā

plain_english: This has already been stated earlier, so it is not examined again; and through further criticisms of external objects, it is rejected.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ caitatpuraiveti na bhūyaḥ pravivicyate bhūyobhiścāpi bāhyārthadūṣaṇaiḥ pravyaramyata

plain_english: Thus this has been determined: the expansion of sound from kalā and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: taditthameṣa nirṇītaḥ kalādervistaro@dhvanaḥ
